newsitem.title: USA: Standard Microsystems sees Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Standard Microsystems sees Q3 loss.

text.p: Standard Microsystems Corp said it now expects to report a loss for the third quarter ending November 30.

The company had originally indicated that it expected a profit for the third quarter, despite a previously announced $4 million charge from the settlement of a legal action with Penril DataComm Networks Inc, Standard Microsystems said.
The change in expectations comes from lower than expected revenues in the company's component products division, Standard Microsystems said.
Standard Microsystems reported a third quarter profit of $303,000, or $0.02 a share, on sales of $90.6 million for the period ended November 30, 1995.
The company anticipates revenues to be higher than the year ago period, but below the $99.2 million reported in the second quarter.
Standard Microsystems said it is experiencing lower than expected orders for input/output integrated circuits from its customers in the Pacific Rim countries.

Also, market analysts have recently reduced their estimates for growth in personal computer shipments for the fourth quarter, Standard Microsystems said. The decline in growth estimates consequently reduces demand for the input output integrated circuits that are used in every personal computer, the company said.
Market prices for these circuits are under pressure, contributing to the decrease in revenues, Standard Microsystems said.
